chunks: DESTROYED WILL BE the hands of Abu Lahab, and he himself will perish.

key_terms.أَبِي لَهَبٍ: Abu Lahab (a specific uncle of the Prophet)
key_terms.يَدَا: The two hands (indicating strength and power)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Tabbat Yada Abi Lahab' in the Quran?
ai.summary: This verse initiates Surah Al-Masad, a Makki surah often cited in Shia tradition as an example of 'tawqifi' (divinely revealed) knowledge, specifically foretelling Abu Lahab's fate despite his initial expectation of immunity due to his wealth and status. It underscores the concept of divine decree against specific disbelievers, highlighting how persistent enmity towards the Prophet Muhammad leads to inevitable spiritual ruin.
